changelog.8e143766c735: Flipcopy behaves as a well-mannered plugin in your DAW. Your project remembers what was on the glass. Scan a few bars straight from the track the copier sits on. Drag a file from the browser straight into a track. Eight copiers at once, at a 256-sample buffer, never crackle.
changelog.ce12abba882c: **Saved with your project.** The original on the glass is kept with your DAW's project, and the glass shows it again when you reopen it. If the file has moved, the glass says *The original has moved*, with **Locate…** to find it. A project whose Flipcopy state can't be read opens with an empty glass and says so; nothing from an earlier project is ever carried over. A newer Flipcopy's settings in a project are kept as they are, so opening a project in an older version and saving it again loses nothing.
changelog.fd7b1afa3b01: **Scan from track.** In a DAW, Copy Settings has *Scan from track*: choose 1 to 16 bars, **Arm**, and press play in your DAW. The track's audio — or the notes it receives — is captured as it plays, written as a new file in your Copies folder's `Captures` folder, and put on the glass. Nothing is copied until you press START. The panel says what a host won't send: Ableton Live gives an audio effect no MIDI, and Logic may not run a track that isn't live.
changelog.222f72339df2: **Drag a file straight into your DAW.** A grip at the end of every audio and MIDI file in the browser, and on the Preview strip, drags the file itself onto a track. The row itself still drags onto the glass.
changelog.38dd0a51f105: **The drag shows the exact clip.** While a page or a file is dragged out to your DAW, the picture under the cursor is that clip — its notes or its waveform — in the lime frame.
changelog.4349d2ea9d2d: **The pianos sound like pianos.** The Grand, Acoustic, Upright and Honky-Tonk pianos — the default toner among them — play Freally MIDI Master's new acoustic voice, built from measurements of a recorded concert grand and upright, with no buzz. A copy you made before keeps the piano it was made with: REPRINT and its ticket make it again exactly as it was.
changelog.4dbfe3c38777: **A piano copy, copied back to MIDI, reads less well for now.** The new pianos ring with real overtones, and the copier can hear them as a line of their own: the melody page may come out an octave or more too high, with the true notes on the countermelody page. Other instruments read as before. A later version teaches the copier to tell a note from its overtones.
changelog.528ac7aef2bf: **Eight copiers at once.** Eight instances, each with its sounds, its preview and a scan running, cost well under one percent of a 256-sample block; an editor with nothing moving runs no animation loop.
changelog.c5bb4099ef7c: **Arrow keys and the mouse wheel move a fader one step, with or without Shift.** A tenth of a decibel is the finest a fader holds; Shift still makes a drag finer.
changelog.489f105e939c: **Two Flipcopy windows opened at once both open.** Opened together — two standalones, or a DAW that runs each plugin in its own process and restores their windows — an editor could stay blank. Fixed in the webview the Freally apps share.
changelog.047de85cd8a2: **No click when your DAW changes its sample rate or buffer size** while the preview plays: the sound comes back in where it was, faded in over five milliseconds.
changelog.ea5df30e60e0: The search for an instrument, and every other thing the window asks of the plugin, is held to a size; a request too large is refused unread.
changelog.ee349e4aa239: A light mode beside the dark one, both in Freally green — and one look, one set of rendered hardware, for every Freally app.
changelog.e47c7e599a1f: **Light and dark.** *Settings → Appearance*: Dark or Light, each shown by its own copier. The change is immediate, with no flash of the other colour, and kept on this computer, the same in the plugin and the standalone. The copier is rendered on each mode's own ground, so it always sits in one room with no box around it.
changelog.b936af04b352: **The Freally look.** The panels, the glass, the dialogs and the keys come from one design shared by every Freally app — modern, sleek and futuristic, in light and in dark — and the knobs, faders, sliders, switches and keys are rendered for each mode.
changelog.8d9fb3f2fece: **The title bar follows the mode.** The standalone's title bar is light in light mode and dark in dark mode, with no title (the turning wordmark is the title).
changelog.58c3153a8c37: **Reduce lays the title flat.** With reduced motion — Flipcopy's own setting, or your system's — the turning title stops square to you, level and flat, rather than held at an angle.
changelog.930a82a2f066: **Quick turns the title faster**: in half the time, as everything Quick speeds up. Reduced motion still wins over both speeds.
changelog.9a34338f7069: **Every key is one width**, in every language, and labels that were too long for it are shorter.
changelog.11bbf02df3a2: **The Studio's play, stop and loop are plain buttons**, as a transport's are.
changelog.27a86b95b65b: **Settings → Sounds says what its switch does**: *Animation sounds* — the sounds of dialogs and panels opening and closing — on or off, beside the machine's own sounds.
changelog.32a3454bd7d7: [0.5.7] — 2026-10-06 — The Mixer and Your Own Instruments
changelog.17791d5cece3: The Studio gets a mixer and a sound for every part. Mix the parts with realistic faders and knobs, shape each instrument with Freally MIDI Master's synth controls, and play the parts through your own samples — a drum kit of your one-shots, or one sample across the keyboard — kept in one instrument library every Freally product on your computer shares.
changelog.79b010c66ef4: **Notes, Mixer and Sound.** Three views in the Studio, side by side at its top; the arrow keys move between them.
changelog.e333eccd6937: **The mixer.** A strip for every part and one for the master: a fader with its meter, pan, solo and mute, and — for a part on a library instrument — MIDI Master's channel strip: Low, Mid and High, Room, Echo, Heat and, for an instrument that sings, Pitch Mod. The meter runs green, then yellow from −12 dBFS, then red from −3, and its clip light comes on at 0 dBFS and stays on until you click it. The mixer is the copy's: what the Studio plays is what START prints, and a part with its fader all the way down is not printed.
changelog.1e76a79a1d7a: **Realistic faders, knobs and keys.** Rendered in Blender for every Freally product: the faders, every knob, the command keys and the toggle keys, with a pressed animation (reduced motion keeps the press without the glow). Drag, hold Shift to move finely, turn the mouse wheel, double-click to go back, or use the keyboard; every one says its value.
changelog.a3541ed53ef6: **Realistic sliders and on/off switches.** Every slider has a gray, grooved thumb on a groove lit up to it, and every on/off setting is a pill switch — lit when it is on, its knob slid to that end, ON or OFF pressed into it. Rendered in Blender with the faders, for dark and light.
changelog.09c5e76649f5: **Every button is a rendered key.** Settings, the licence agreement, the browser and the Studio use the same Blender keys as the copier, with their press, and keys that sit together are all one width.
changelog.1f83f75b3bdd: **A part's sound.** The library instrument with Freally MIDI Master's SYNTH page — oscillators, sub and noise, filter, both envelopes, LFOs, macros and effects — kept with the copy's settings; Reset puts it back.
changelog.e93b9221b8bd: **Your own samples.** Select an audio file in the browser and press *Add to your samples*. A sample is a file on this computer, up to 20 seconds; its pitch is read as it is added, and it is checked again every time it plays, so a sample that has moved or changed is never played as something else.
changelog.8f95a81b18c2: **Your own drum kit.** *New kit*, then a one-shot on each lane — chosen from your samples or dragged from the browser onto the lane.
changelog.4f44482071a3: **The simple sampler.** One of your samples across the keyboard for a part, with its root note, tuning, envelope, filter and volume.
changelog.26e0f4686505: **Favourites.** A star on any instrument, drum machine, sample, kit or sampler sound; the *Starred* list plays one on the part.
changelog.d16f22a46ceb: **One instrument library for every Freally product** on this computer. Flipcopy ships no samples: yours are read where they are.
changelog.09f42e7fbf57: **Copy Settings says what the copy plays**: a part on one of your sampler sounds, the drums on your kit, and a mixer set in the Studio — with a button to reset it.
changelog.30e9ac21e3ee: Choosing a part's instrument starts it as itself: the knobs moved on the instrument before, and a sampler sound, are let go.
changelog.64c277607a3c: **Waveforms drawn from the sound itself.** The preview's waveform — and the picture a file carries when it is dragged — is read from the file's own samples, every column its true peaks and its loudness, drawn as a DAW draws one: the peaks as a soft outline round a solid body. A short one-shot had drawn as a few flat blocks.
changelog.df0a41720e80: **A maximized window is filled.** Maximized or made bigger, the standalone showed the app at the size it opened at, with a white edge beside it; now the whole window is the app, scaled as one.
changelog.b75b41a222c5: In Arabic, the Studio's SEND TO THE COPIER key sits at the end of its row again.
changelog.8b3ee24a5a5b: A second tab beside the copier. Open a copy in the **Studio** and each of its parts is a tab in MIDI Master's own piano roll: change the notes, hear them through the instruments the copy prints with, and send the edit back to the glass — where the green START makes a new copy of it that drags into your DAW.
changelog.05f4a806504e: **COPIER and STUDIO.** Two tabs above the machine — `Ctrl+1` and `Ctrl+2` (`Cmd` on a Mac) from anywhere, or the arrows between them. Switching never stops anything: a copy being scanned carries on behind the Studio, and its pages are out when you come back. Each instance keeps its own tab.
changelog.c3cc9f721474: **Open in Studio.** The touch screen's **STUDIO** key opens the copy in the tray; in the browser, **Open in Studio** opens the copy of a file you select in Copies. A copy of an audio loop opens its MIDI pages, one tab each in page order; an audio copy opens the parts of the MIDI it was made from. The notes are read from the files the copy wrote — a copy whose files have moved or changed is refused, and the Studio says why.
changelog.93f13976feb6: **MIDI Master's piano roll.** Draw a note with a double-click; drag a note to move it; drag its left edge `[` or its right edge `]` to lengthen or shorten it; box-select, Shift- and Ctrl-click; copy, cut, paste, clone (`Shift+D`, or drag with Alt), delete (Delete, Backspace, or a right-click); nudge with the arrows; the velocity lane underneath; snap; undo and redo. Drums show their kit voices by name down the side.
changelog.71cc9842a84d: **Hear it.** PLAY, STOP and LOOP, and a solo and a mute on every part. What plays is exactly the file the copier will be given, through the instruments the copy prints with — change a part's instrument right there. A part you solo sounds exactly as its page of the copy will, whatever else is muted.
changelog.118cc9125c81: **Send to the copier.** The edit is written as a new MIDI file in your Copies folder's `Studio` folder — never over another — and put on the glass. Press START and it is copied like any original; its ticket says which copy it was edited from.
changelog.9ee308e27a53: **The fan of pages is wider.** Every page under the top one shows its left and front edges, wide enough to Shift-click and grab; a page you raise goes to the top of the pile and the pages under it close up. A Shift-click picks a page without moving the pile.
changelog.14a8f0896eef: **A one-part MIDI file is copied as the part its name says.** A file of a single line named for its part — `…-Bass.mid`, `… - Countermelody - …` — is copied as that part, through that part's instrument, rather than guessed from how high or low it sits.
changelog.ba657b6bc761: A long row of buttons under a selected file in the browser could push the browser under the copier; it now wraps.
changelog.0f03db88ad85: A file the copier writes is never written over another that a second copier (another instance of Flipcopy in your DAW) saved under the same name a moment before; it takes the next free name.
changelog.63f032bc62d6: The copier's touch screen comes alive. **Copy Settings** opens out of it — which parts to copy, the grid, the swing, the tempo, the instruments, the format — and every setting changes the copy you make; the screen's keys page through your copies, save them, show them and print them again; and a copy can go back on the glass to be copied the other way.
changelog.fe9572610f3a: **Copy Settings.** Press **SETTINGS** on the touch screen and the panel grows out of it. For an audio loop: copy **every part**, one part **only** (drums, bassline, melody or chords — refused, never a blank page, when the loop has none of it), or the **vocal line**, read as one note at a time; put the notes on a **grid** (1/8, 1/16, 1/32 or 1/16T) and **straighten** a swing. For a MIDI file: a page per part, or the **mix only**; an **instrument** for each part — search the library by name, genre or family — and a **drum machine** (808, 909, 707, 606); the **tail** after the last note; **WAV**, **AIFF**, **FLAC** or **MP3** (320 kbps), at 44.1, 48, 88.2 or 96 kHz, in 16, 24 or 32-bit float. Both ways: the **tempo** — automatic, the project's, the file's own, the file name's, or one you set. Changes are for the next copy, never one being made, and the project keeps them.
changelog.80133c005eb5: **Every page says its instrument** on its TONER line, beside its tempo and where that tempo came from.
changelog.54c5f05f9607: **The file name's tempo, offered.** A MIDI file with no tempo of its own whose name says one (*Hook 127 BPM.mid*) gets a chip by the screen: *Use 127 BPM* copies that file at it; the project's tempo never moves.
changelog.762dc63396b4: **The stack.** ◀ **PREV** and **NEXT** ▶ (or `[` and `]`) page through your copies, each lying in the tray ready to drag; **SAVE** saves the page on top as a new file, in the format you pick; **REVEAL** shows it in its folder; **REPRINT** puts the copy's original back on the glass with the settings it was made with — press START to make it again.
changelog.5e9b6523831f: **A copy of a copy.** A page dragged back onto the glass — or dropped from your Copies — goes on as an original, and the new copy says which page it came from.
changelog.9c72fd49cbf7: **Several pages at once.** Shift-click pages to pick them; drag one and they all go, in page order.
changelog.c754df195ab0: **The ticket.** Every copy's folder holds a `ticket.txt`: the original and its fingerprint, the settings, the tempo and where it came from, the instruments, the session it was made in, and every page's file and fingerprint. `flipc copy --ticket` makes the same copy again, byte for byte.
changelog.14e910f0a79b: **Settings.** Speed (**Quick** runs the machine short), **Reduced motion** (follow the system, or always), the **Copies folder** (**Change…** and **Show in folder** — new copies go to the new folder, old ones stay where they are), the interface sounds' own switch, and About's licences and agreement.
changelog.54aac57413aa: **Interface sounds.** Settings, Copy Settings and the browser open, close, hide and show with short, soft, glassy sounds, each exactly as long as its move — through the plugin's own output, never into a bounce, and off with their own switch.
changelog.b58b14c86e76: **A page under the top one** can be pressed where it shows past the tray's edge.
changelog.b0befc5e6040: [0.4.0] — 2026-10-05 — The file browser and the preview player
changelog.e884ffe2f90e: Find a sample or a MIDI clip, hear it, see it, and put it on the glass — the browser and the preview player from Freally Oscillate, beside the copier. Everything essential is here: the MVP is complete.
changelog.130b73a201db: **The browser.** It opens on its Categories — **Copies**, every page and mix you have made, and **Recent**, the originals you last put on the glass, each counted — then the folders you add with **+ Add Folder** (up to 128). A folder on a drive that is unplugged keeps its place and says so; right-click a folder, or select it and press `Delete`, to stop browsing it, and nothing on disk is touched. **Back** and **Forward** move through where you have been, exactly as in Freally Oscillate.
changelog.3c76294f691c: **A folder as a tree.** Expand and collapse it, type to filter it, narrow it to a tag or to your stars, and choose **Show all files** to see the sidecar files it hides (`.asd`, `.reapeaks` and the like). `↑`/`↓` walk the rows and each one you land on plays once; `→` opens a folder, `←` closes it, and `Enter` puts the file on the glass.
changelog.9e19fd75f5c5: **Indexing you can watch.** A new folder is counted on a thread of its own with a bar that shows how far it has got — at most 12 folders deep and 50,000 files, never following a shortcut out of the folder.
changelog.7e5083732503: **The preview player**, docked under the browser. Audio shows its real waveform; a MIDI file shows its notes and plays through **Preview Piano**, the very sound and render a copy uses, so the preview is the copy. `Space` plays and pauses; click or drag the strip to move the playhead, which counts to the music's last note, never the bar line; loop, play-when-selected and a level. A WAV of any length streams; another format plays if it is five minutes or shorter. It plays through the plugin's own output and never into a bounce.
changelog.ca065d9e7b42: **Hear the copy before it goes.** Click the original on the glass or any page on the tray to preview it; when a copy is done, **Copy** plays every page together and **Original** plays the glass, from the same place in the music. Optional: the pages drag the moment the last one lands, played or not.
changelog.d17537ff40ec: **Drag to the glass.** A row, or the preview strip — framed in the same lime as a page — dragged onto the copier puts that file on the glass, with a mini-print of it following the pointer. Nothing starts until START.
changelog.cda58c5f73eb: **Hide the browser** with `Ctrl+B` (`Cmd+B` on a Mac) or the button at its edge: the stage takes the whole window and the turning title re-centres. Flipcopy remembers it.
changelog.5d236e4be21d: **Report a problem, from the app.** When Flipcopy itself fails, the screen offers **Report**, which opens the report page in your web browser showing exactly what it holds; nothing is sent unless you press Send there.
changelog.49de87a64bae: **The docs site** is built from the shared Freally site kit, the same on every Freally site, with its manual updated for this version.
changelog.b0f81c543dda: **A page under the pointer is found at any window size.** A click or a drag on a page landed in the wrong place once the window was scaled.
changelog.df6f06284fdc: Put an audio loop on the glass, press START, and its MIDI comes out — one page for every layer the copier hears, back to back from one scan, each its own file, framed in lime and dragged into your DAW on its own or all together. A MIDI file with several parts comes out the same way: one audio page per part, and the whole file as one mix.
changelog.24a7fe5481b4: **Audio → MIDI.** An audio loop is read into its layers — drums, bass, melody, a **countermelody** where the loop has a second, independent line, and chords — with MIDI Master's classic-DSP extractor (no AI). Each layer found is its own page and its own `.mid`, named as a DAW shows it (*Loop - Bassline - 120 BPM - C# Minor*); a layer that isn't there gets no page, and a loop with no notes at all is refused rather than copied blank. The key is printed only when it was read clearly.
changelog.0c3d252fc872: **A stack of pages.** The pages eject one after another from the single scan, fanned on the tray, each titled by its form and its part (*MIDI MELODY*, *AUDIO BASSLINE*) with *PAGE n/N*. Click a page to bring it to the top. **Nothing drags until the last page has landed.**
changelog.55fa665ebb50: **Two drags from the finished stack.** The top page carries two lime tabs: **All parts** drags every page as separate files, so the DAW lays them out as one track per layer; **Complete mix** drags one file of everything — a multi-track `.mid` of every part, or the whole render as a `.wav` — written beside the pages and never printed. Hover the tab for the mix's facts; without a pointer, *Save the complete mix as…* saves it.
changelog.7ab067eeb165: **MIDI → audio, part by part.** A MIDI file with several parts prints one audio page per part (*AUDIO MELODY*, *AUDIO BASSLINE*), each rendered on its own and drawn from its own WAV, plus the Complete mix — the parts sum to the mix, under one headroom gain.
changelog.71cfe75f90c6: **Loops of up to 16 bars.** The glass refuses a longer clip with its length in bars, never cutting it short; a one-, two- or four-bar loop is still copied. An audio loop's bars are counted at the tempo the copier reads it at.
changelog.6aed786b024a: **Honest pages.** A Chords page says it is a progression, not the played voicing; when a sung line was heard and left alone, the first page says so, and a loop that is only a sung line is refused saying that, not "nothing to copy". Every tempo printed names where it came from — read from the loop, or, when the loop's hits fit no grid, the host's, the file name's or the default.
changelog.cb05cd0fc0f0: **`flipc`**, the command line, running the plugin's own glass and copier: `flipc copy <file> --out <dir>`, `flipc facts <file>` (the data block exactly as the paper prints it), `flipc score` (the corpus scorer) and `flipc bench` (timings).
changelog.d2365b73e8bc: **The corpus gate.** The audioTest corpus is scored on every local CI run where it is present — and says SKIPPED where it isn't — against floors that only rise.
changelog.d2a673b21c8f: **The host's tempo is followed block by block**, and a MIDI file with no tempo of its own is copied at the host's tempo at the moment you press START.
changelog.ee270218636c: **The session tempo only breaks the octave tie.** A 120 BPM loop dropped in a 90 BPM session is read at 120 (four bars), not at 90 (three) — fixed in MIDI Master's shared extractor, for every Freally product that reads loops.
changelog.ab8ac52d964e: **Free today, not promised forever.** Freally Flipcopy is free today, but it might not be free forever: future versions may be sold. Every page of the docs site now says so.
changelog.7fb464e21cf8: **The repository moved** to the maintainer's own GitHub account, private and All Rights Reserved, with the shared Freally crates coming from Freally MIDI Master and Freally Oscillate beside it; the plugin's web address is the docs site's new one.
changelog.c584da8d5dfd: **Continuous integration runs on the maintainer's machine** before every push — every gate on Windows, and the Linux gates in Docker Desktop — and none on GitHub Actions. Every commit carries `[skip ci]`. (For a few hours on 2026-09-30, the repository was public and CI ran on GitHub for every push.)
changelog.79a07e8925af: **The editor keeps its own browser profile.** Flipcopy's WebView2 data (`%APPDATA%\Freally Flipcopy\webview`) had been filed under Freally MIDI Master's folder, and two products sharing one WebView2 profile can leave each other's editor blank when both run in the same DAW. It is Flipcopy's own now.
changelog.72de476110e3: **A copy's Complete mix can only ever be its own file**: a `record.json` edited behind the copier can't point a drag, a Save As or a Reveal anywhere else.
changelog.427549a6dab4: **A copy is written whole or not at all.** Every page and the mix are on disk before any of them takes its name, so a failure part-way never leaves pages in a numbered folder that no copy owns.
changelog.2604a6288e96: **No page clips.** The one headroom gain is set by every file a copy writes — a part can peak above the mix where the others cancel it.
changelog.c6cb2c38dd63: **A 16-bar loop exported a tick long is 16 bars**, not 17 — a last note released a thirty-second past the bar line is not a bar of its own.
changelog.2ba628500475: **Controllers reach a page** even on a channel that plays no notes.
changelog.833039ba4e85: [0.2.0] — 2026-09-30 — The copier and the first copy
changelog.35409a92a233: The copier stands on the stage, playing the Blender copier story videos' beats in their order: drop a MIDI file on the glass, press the green START, and a real audio copy comes out onto the tray — printed from its own file, framed in lime, and dragged straight into your DAW.
changelog.c12f4045ef96: **The copier on the stage.** The machine rendered by the same Blender scene as the two story videos — its base, its lid as sprite frames, the pressed keys, the glass and tray mattes — rendered over the window's own ground (`#090c09`) on transparent film, so it stands in the room with no seam. The phases are the videos' beats in the videos' order (the sheet flips and lands face-down, the lid swings shut with its bounce, the START beep, the lamp sweeps side to side leaking cyan out of the front seam while the whole room dims, the copy slides out onto the tray), at the in-app cut's shorter durations; a test fails if the app ever plays a beat the story doesn't have, skips one, or plays them out of order. It fills whatever room the window gives it and never mirrors in a right-to-left language.
changelog.81d392181aa1: **The green START is the only trigger.** Dropping a clip only puts it on the glass. START (or `Ctrl/Cmd+Enter`, which presses the same key) starts the copy; STOP (or `Esc`) cancels it mid-scan with nothing left behind; HOME clears the glass. The key carries an angled *START*, turned to the touch panel, and its LED is lit whenever a copy can start. A plugin test sends every command and fails if any but `copier_start` starts a job, and a build gate fails if the page ever sends it from anywhere but the START key.
changelog.3c73db8b1385: **The glass.** Drop an audio or MIDI file from Explorer or Finder anywhere on the window (the glass lights up as it arrives), or press `Enter` on the empty glass to pick one. It is read on a thread of its own and printed face-up before it lands — the real notes or the real waveform, with the file's own facts. Network paths, oversized, over-long, silent, damaged, SMPTE-timed and format-2 MIDI files are each refused with their own sentence. Two files at once: the first goes on, and the machine says one clip at a time. A new clip dropped on a finished copy is laid on the glass the same way, and the tray clears (the copy stays in the Copies folder). A file the glass refuses leaves the clip that was on it where it is.
changelog.4267b3fd96ac: **MIDI → audio.** The copy renders the file's notes through a default toner — MIDI Master's own preset voices for the pitched parts and a drum machine, one voice per GM lane, for the drums — honouring pitch bend and the sustain pedal (each channel's on that channel's notes only), with a 2.5 s tail, at the file's tempo (else the host's — the standalone has none — else the one in the file name, else 120 — and the page names which), kept under −0.3 dBFS, and written as a 24-bit WAV at the host's sample rate (44.1 kHz in the standalone) that a DAW places on the beat grid. A copy is as long as a page can be printed from — five minutes, or 2:30 above 48 kHz — and a longer one is refused before it is rendered, never cut short. Audio → MIDI arrives at `v0.3.0`; until then START on an audio clip says so, honestly.
changelog.d9714ba71fa5: **The Copies folder** (`Documents/Freally Flipcopy/Copies`): one numbered folder per copy, taken atomically so two DAWs never share a number; pages named the way a DAW shows them (`Title - Part - 120 BPM, Key.wav`); every page written atomically, read back and verified — and **never moved, overwritten or deleted**, because your DAW refers to it by its path.
changelog.48b3f94d470b: **Prints, from the files themselves.** Every page — the original on the glass and the copy in the tray — is laser-printed like the story videos' prints: title, source line, bar ruler, the piano roll with its velocity lane or the waveform with its new **spectrum strip**, and the data block, all computed by the plugin from the bytes on disk. A bar of an odd meter keeps its half beat (7/8 prints three and a half beats a bar). A copy's page says what its render left out — controllers it did not play, drum notes the kit has no voice for — never dropping them quietly. A test reads the structure of the app's pages and of the videos' own prints and holds them to each other.
changelog.fa6958b17901: **Drag the copy into your DAW.** The ejected page wears a lime frame round its clip with *Drag to DAW* beneath it — the frame is the handle. Press inside it and move 4 px, and the copy's own file is dragged (with a mini print on the cursor) into FL Studio, Ableton, Reaper or any DAW that takes files. Nothing drags until the page is fully out; where no drag can be made here, the frame turns grey and dashed and offers Save As instead. `Enter` on the page opens Save As or shows the file in its folder.
changelog.4da7005c5000: **The machine's sounds**, synthesised from scratch for this copier (place, lid, beep, scan start, one whir per lamp sweep, eject) and mixed by the plugin into its own output — never an HTML `<audio>` — at −18 dB through the Monitor level, quiet while your DAW plays (the standalone has no DAW transport to be quiet for), silent in an offline bounce, and never in place of your track's audio. Settings has them on/off, their level, and the "quiet while playing" choice.
changelog.f8fc9e0d2e58: **The touch screen** shows what the machine is doing, the clip it holds, and every refusal in the producer's language.
changelog.1a5ee7d7aabc: **Gates** for all of it, each watched failing before it was trusted: the ground-match trio (the render's colours equal the tokens; ΔE2000 around the machine's own alpha silhouette in every phase at DPR 1 and 2; nothing between the machine and the ground paints), the START gate (static, plugin and Playwright), print parity, the drag frame's pixels, and the new app-leg specs in the real standalone.
changelog.66b1e687636a: **Shared code**: `freally-extract` (the decode door and the audio analysis), `freally-encode` (WAV, resampling, the DAW-grid chunks) and `freally-drag` (the native drag source) are consumed from MIDI Master at `shared-v5`, with `freally_library::audition::NoteRenderer`, `read_facts`' controller events, and the web view adapter's file-drop hook, its re-placing of the web view when the window moves and its blank caption added upstream there.
changelog.e7908191194e: **The icon is the owner's own** — the lime *F* over a waveform and a piano roll — on the executable, the plugin bundles, the Linux and macOS icons and the docs site, in place of the placeholder.
changelog.719f74499130: **The window.** The standalone's title bar wears the icon, is dark and the colour of the room, and says nothing: no title in the title bar of the standalone or of a plugin window in a DAW whose caption names Flipcopy, since the turning name across the top of the window already says it. That turning name is twice the size, to be read at a glance, and centred over the copier's side of the window; the file browser runs from the top of the window to the preview dock beside it.
changelog.120afa46c010: The bridge takes requests up to 2 MiB (a drag image); `host_info` says whether a page can be dragged here.
changelog.df29ffbf7480: Before the licence agreement is accepted, the page can read the interface language and nothing else, through a command of its own (`locale_get`); `prefs_get` answers only once it is accepted.
changelog.bf4a28a43b62: **Moving the window on a scaled display.** With Windows set to 150 %, dragging the standalone window by its title bar drew its contents a third of the way behind the window, towards the screen's top-left corner, hiding the right and bottom edges until the window was moved back to that corner. The contents now stay exactly under the window wherever it is moved.
changelog.f246f03536b6: **The standalone at your display's own scale.** On a scaled display (150 %) the standalone ran as an old-style, unscaled program: Windows stretched its window while the page inside it drew at true pixels — the root of the drag and drop-down misplacements listed here. It now declares itself per-monitor DPI aware before it opens a window, as Freally MIDI Master's and Freally Unloop's standalones do, so the page draws crisply at the display's scale and the window opens at its intended size.
changelog.4d43aa80977a: **The language list opens under its field.** On a scaled display the system's own drop-down list opened down and to the right of the Settings field, further off the further the field sat from the window's corner; the list is now drawn by Flipcopy itself, straight under the field, in the window's own dark style, with each language written in its own script.
changelog.8847996db9e9: The empty product every later rung builds on: it loads, passes audio through untouched, asks for the licence agreement, opens its dark window, and every quality gate runs.
changelog.cc29ebe17a90: **The plugin, in every format from one binary.** A nih-plug CLAP plugin with VST3 and AUv2 entry points projected by `clap-wrapper` (licence-clean: no GPL VST3 bindings), plus the **standalone application** — a native desktop app with its own window and audio device, never a web app. Stereo in and out, a note input for the later "Scan from track", zero latency, and the track's audio passed through **bit for bit** (a null test proves it). A host **Bypass** switch and a **Monitor** level for the sound Flipcopy itself will add (the machine's sounds and the preview, from `v0.2.0`) — it never touches the track. A versioned saved state that is bounded, migrated and refused as a whole rather than half-loaded, so a damaged project never crashes the host.
changelog.59616adfaedb: **The licence agreement** (`EULA.md`, structured like Freally Oscillate's) and its gate: Flipcopy asks you to accept it on first open and stays inert until you do — it reads nothing, copies nothing and adds nothing to your track. The agreement is compiled into the plugin and served from it, Agree waits until the text has been read to the end, and your answer is shared by every open instance and the standalone. A decline that could not be saved says so.
changelog.ed5631790156: **The window**, opening at 1400 × 875 (Freally Unloop's size) and scaling as one to any size — everything keeps its proportions, with no band around it — under a title bar where *Freally Flipcopy* and its version turn on the Y axis in 3D, the same way Freally Oscillate's and Freally MIDI Master's do (and stand still for reduced motion): the dark shell with the browser rail and the preview dock on the inline-start side, a draggable splitter (260–420 px, arrow keys too), and the stage — which has no background of its own, so the copier will stand in the room with no seam around it. One theme, dark, and nothing that could make a second one.
changelog.ccf91016802f: **Eighteen languages** for everything in the window, with the choice saved per computer and shared by every instance; right-to-left layouts for Arabic.
changelog.92d766745704: **Google's Noto fonts**, vendored into the bundle under the SIL Open Font License 1.1, with the licence shipped beside them.
changelog.b502e66ba7a3: **The docs site**, built like Freally Oscillate's and dark-only, in the same eighteen languages (each loaded only when a reader picks it): the home page with the version ladder (generated from `docs/ladder.json` and held to the private plan by a gate), the two Blender copier stories in "See it copy", the documentation, this changelog, and a download page that says plainly there is nothing to download before `v1.0.0`. The stories play with their sound, only when you press the angled START on the copier's green key (or play), and come to rest on their first frame when they end or are stopped; the audio → MIDI story prints a page per layer — MIDI Melody, MIDI Chords, MIDI Bassline and MIDI Countermelody — one after another onto a stack in the tray, each framed in lime with *Drag to DAW* beneath it.
changelog.96a59e69b7f8: **Text stays inside its containers** in all 18 languages, at the default window and the smallest one (a Playwright check over every label).
changelog.495bcdf8956e: **The gates**, each watched failing before it was trusted: formatting, clippy, every test, type checks, lint, the locale gate (18 catalogs, identical keys and placeholders, actually translated), the logical-CSS lint, design tokens and contrast, dark-only, the denylist (no AI, no network, no telemetry), the licence audit, the shared-crate gate (consume, never fork), product names (never a copier maker's trademark), bindings drift, the ladder, no downloads before 1.0, the asset budget, `clap-validator` and `pluginval` at strictness 10, local CI on Windows and in Docker for Linux, and Playwright on two legs — the browser and the real standalone window.
changelog.09dd8d0ea4e1: The editor loads only the page compiled into the binary, under a strict Content Security Policy; its bridge answers only the page's own JSON `POST`, refuses anything over 64 KiB and any path with `..`, and before the agreement is accepted answers only an allowlist of commands. Release builds open no DevTools and no remote-debugging port.
changelog.e06fbd4d3359: No network code in the plugin or the standalone, checked by the compiler (`clippy.toml`) and the dependency graph (`scripts/check-denylist.mjs`).
changelog.70e17daefb45: The files Flipcopy keeps in your app-data folder (the agreement answer and the preferences) are read with a size bound and written atomically, so a damaged or hand-edited file loads as the defaults and a crash never leaves half a file.
